lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 4 you ran, jumped and threw in athletics. Which is timed with a stopwatch: a sprint or a jump? (A sprint.) Today: a sprint start, a relay handover and jumping technique.
The crouch start. 'On your marks': front foot in the front block, back knee on the ground. Hands just behind the start line, arms straight, shoulders over the hands, eyes down.
'Set': lift the hips to just above the shoulders, knees bent, and hold still. On the gun, drive hard out of the blocks, stay low for a few strides, pump the arms, then rise gradually.
A 4 × 100 m relay: four runners carry a baton. The next runner starts when the incoming runner reaches a check mark. The baton must change hands inside the 30 m takeover zone.

The handover: the incoming runner calls 'Hand!' The next runner reaches back with a steady, open hand, without looking, and the baton is pushed firmly into it. The baton goes right hand, left hand, right, left.
Long jump: a fast, even run-up, take off from one foot, knees up in the air, land feet first and fall forwards. It is measured from the take-off line to the nearest mark in the sand.
The triple jump: a hop (take off and land on the same foot) and a step (land on the other foot). Then a jump: land on both feet in the pit. Add the three: 3.5 + 2.5 + 3 = 9 m.

Try it in the world: build a track with a yellow takeover zone, and a sand pit with a take-off board. For real: practise the crouch start and a handover with a friend, and measure your jumps. Next: analyse and improve.

exercises.prompt: Put the starter's words in order.
exercises.hint: The first words get you into the blocks.
exercises.explain: 'On your marks', then 'Set', then the gun.

exercises.prompt: In 'On your marks', where are your hands?
exercises.hint: Touching the line is not allowed.
exercises.explain: Just behind the start line, arms straight.

exercises.prompt: A 4 × 100 m relay team has four runners.
From where is a long jump measured?
exercises.hint: It is measured from the board to the sand.
exercises.explain: From the take-off line to the nearest mark in the sand.

exercises.prompt: What does the sprinter do in the 'Set' position?
exercises.hint: Look at the hips and the shoulders.
choices: lift the hips just above the shoulders
exercises.explain: In 'Set', the hips rise just above the shoulders, ready to drive.

exercises.prompt: A relay team's four legs took 14 s, 15 s, 13 s and 16 s. What was the team's time, in seconds?
The baton may be passed anywhere on the track.
exercises.hint: Look at the yellow box on the relay picture.
exercises.explain: False: it must be passed inside the 30 m takeover zone.

exercises.prompt: The heels land at 3.4 m, but a hand falls back to 3.1 m. How long is the jump, in metres?
exercises.hint: Measure to the nearest mark in the sand.
exercises.explain: The nearest mark is the hand at 3.1 m, so the jump is 3.1 m.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of the triple jump to how you land.
matches: on both feet in the pit
exercises.hint: Hop on one foot, step to the other, jump into the sand.
exercises.explain: Hop: land on the same foot. Step: land on the other foot. Jump: land on both feet in the pit.

exercises.prompt: What does the incoming relay runner call to the next runner?
exercises.hint: It tells the next runner to reach back.
exercises.explain: 'Hand!': the signal to reach back for the baton.

exercises.prompt: Zara's triple jump: a hop of 3.2 m, a step of 2.6 m and a jump of 2.9 m. How far is it, in metres?
Why does the next relay runner start running before the baton arrives?
exercises.hint: What speed should the baton keep?
choices: so both are running fast at the handover
to get a head start in the race
exercises.explain: So both runners are at full speed when the baton changes hands.

exercises.prompt: Why should a long jumper fall forwards on landing?
exercises.hint: Remember how a jump is measured.
choices: a mark behind the feet makes the jump shorter
exercises.explain: The jump is measured to the nearest mark: falling back makes a mark closer to the board.

exercises.prompt: Put the long jump in order.
exercises.hint: Speed first, then leave the ground.

exercises.prompt: A jump where the foot goes over the take-off line is a no-jump, and does not count.
exercises.hint: Where must the take-off foot be?
exercises.explain: True: stepping over the line is a no-jump.

exercises.prompt: Mimi's long jumps: 3.24 m, a no-jump and 3.41 m. What is her best jump that counts, in metres?
exercises.hint: A no-jump never counts. Compare the others.
exercises.explain: The no-jump does not count, so the best is 3.41 m.
